tagline: Gravel roads parallel wagon ruts through sagebrush valleys and juniper ranges.
intro: California Trail Back Country Byway crosses sagebrush valleys, juniper-covered ranges, springs and streams in northern Elko County. BLM lists it as a Type I Back Country Byway and gives it 96 miles, with at least three hours for travel. Its historical value lies beside the drive: wagon ruts survive where the modern route parallels part of the California National Historic Trail.

In 1843, Joseph Walker led a California-bound wagon party across Thousand Springs Valley and down Bishop Creek to the Humboldt River. An 1845 route variant through Humboldt Wells later diverted traffic from that original connection. The byway also traces part of a different transport route, the Magic City Freight Line between Toano, Nevada, and what is now Twin Falls, Idaho.

Begin off US 93 north of Wells; BLM’s brochure places an information kiosk four miles into the byway near Winecup Ranch. From the ranch toward Little Goose Creek, more than 40 miles of road parallel the historic trail.

moments.title: Thousand Springs approach
moments.text: The byway is reached near the turnoff to Thousand Springs, a watering place for emigrants traveling through this country. The Oregon-California Trails Association traces an 1843 wagon party across Thousand Springs Valley with Joseph Walker, then down Bishop Creek to the Humboldt.

moments.title: Winecup Ranch interpretation
moments.text: BLM’s brochure places a history kiosk near Winecup Ranch, four miles into the byway from US 93. Winecup also marks one end of the long section that parallels the California National Historic Trail toward Little Goose Creek.

moments.title: Toward Little Goose Creek
moments.text: The stretch from Winecup Ranch to Little Goose Creek parallels the historic trail for more than 40 miles. Recreation.gov identifies surviving wagon ruts along the byway, as well as the separate freight-line connection between Toano and Twin Falls. The landscape includes broad sagebrush valleys and juniper-covered mountain ranges.

practical: Thousand Springs approach: Recreation.gov reports rough roads and missing directional signs, recommends high clearance, and advises avoiding wet or snowy conditions. (checked 2026-10-20)
